ratio_scope_caution: The 6/8 ratio describes only Merrill's published illustrative <tsch> set, not the historical lexicon as a whole; the pinned modern lexicon is not a dialectally balanced sample.
selection_independence: All eight illustrative historical <tsch> lexemes in Merrill §7.5.2 were audited by modern semantic/domain retrieval. Positive graphic-semantic, semantic non-graphic, unresolved, and graphic-decoy outcomes are retained.

patterns.interpretation: Strong documentary recurrence in the participial/derivational domain; not automatic morphological identity or cognacy.

patterns.specific_modern_phonemic_holdout: Caballero 2022 /tʃaˈpí/ 'grab' corresponds semantically to historical tschapí 'agarrar' and modern Chapí RD-000656.
patterns.interpretation: The full published illustrative <tsch> set yields six semantic-modern matches supporting ch, one semantic match without ch support, and one unresolved domain. The multi-family recurrence is compatible with published historical and modern phonetic analyses, but no sound law or cognacy is adjudicated.

patterns.published_historical_phonetic_interpreta: Merrill et al. 2020 treats intervocalic <ss> as voiceless [s], not phonological gemination.

patterns.interpretation: Observed in Cotſchimé~Cochí but also in semantically contradictory Bajé~Bají; cannot discriminate continuity.

source_supported_interpretation.steffel_tsch: Merrill et al. 2020 §7.5.2 associates <tsch> with a voiceless palatoalveolar affricate [č] and analyzes <tsch>/<ts> as allophones of /č/; Appendix 5 systematically transcribes <tsch> with č.
source_supported_interpretation.steffel_ss: Merrill et al. 2020 §7.5.5 interprets intervocalic <ss> as voiceless [s], not phonological gemination.
source_supported_interpretation.modern_choguita: Caballero 2022 includes phonemic /tʃ/ and /s/, optional /tʃ/→[ts] depalatalization before low central vowels, and independently documents /tʃaˈpí/ 'grab'.
source_supported_interpretation.structural_parallel: Historical initial <tsch>/<ts> free variation before a and modern optional /tʃ/→[ts] before low central vowels constitute a source-supported allophonic structural parallel, not proof that one historical conditioning rule persisted unchanged.
source_supported_interpretation.variety_caution: Choguita Rarámuri and the pinned SRC-02 lexicon are independent modern sources/varieties and are not collapsed into one variety.
